comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C17-C22 regarding functional RNA-responsive CRISPR activation in mammalian cells. Both evaluations find the data convincing and support the principle of the system with synthetic triggers in cell culture.

Perfect agreement on claims C23-C31 regarding iterative design improvements and extended trigger detection. Both acknowledge the success of second-generation designs and detection of longer triggers, with peer reviewers noting variable performance that OpenEval also recognizes.

Strong agreement on claims C34-C44, C108-C111 regarding modular design and MODesign algorithm. Both evaluations support the computational tool and modular strategy as valid contributions with high potential, acknowledging the experimental validation data.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C48-C60, C75, C77, C112 regarding the RNA cleavage mechanism. Both evaluations accept the mechanistic work as demonstrated by circularization assays and gel electrophoresis data, confirming the cleavage-based activation mechanism.

Divergent evaluations on claims C2, C61-C73, C82-C83 regarding in vivo application. OpenEval finds the data robustly SUPPORTED with statistical validation, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting 'subtle' and 'encouraging' but modest effects requiring further optimization.

Partial overlap on claims C4, C64-C67 regarding chemical modifications. OpenEval finds the rational design SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers include these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of overall in vivo work, focusing on the modest effect sizes rather than the design logic.

Agreement on claims C74, C114-C116 regarding CRISPRa component optimization. Both evaluations support the systematic testing and trade-offs between activator strength and background noise, treating this as valid experimental optimization.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for claims C13, C81 regarding novelty and field limitations. Both recognize these as subjective assessments that cannot be fully verified, though peer reviewers acknowledge the work as 'a reasonable starting point' and 'important for many in the field.'

Partial overlap on claims C11-C12 regarding prior work limitations. OpenEval rates these UNCERTAIN as subjective field assessments, while peer reviewers implicitly support the optimization work that addresses these limitations.
Agreement on claims C5-C10 as SUPPORTED background knowledge. Both evaluations accept these established contextual claims supported by citations without challenge.

Agreement on claims C14-C16, C113 as SUPPORTED background knowledge. Both evaluations treat these as established facts appropriately cited, providing necessary context but not representing novel findings.

Partial overlap on claims C45-C47, C54, C76 regarding RNAi pathway context. OpenEval includes these in SUPPORTED mechanistic evaluation, while peer reviewers treat them as uncontested background claims in their SUPPORTED category.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for claims C84-C95 regarding future applications and optimization. Both recognize these as speculative claims about potential uses, with peer reviewers noting 'myriad opportunities' but emphasizing need for 'future studies and experiments.'

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for claims C103, C105-C107 regarding therapeutic applications with endogenous triggers. Peer reviewers explicitly identify this as 'the weakness of the study' - lack of demonstration in 'completely natural setting' with endogenous transcripts.

Partial overlap on claims C96-C102, C104 regarding CRISPR safety and delivery. OpenEval rates discussion as UNCERTAIN speculation, while peer reviewers treat the background context (safety concerns, delivery challenges) as SUPPORTED established knowledge.

Minimal overlap on claim C86 regarding optimization needs. OpenEval includes this in UNCERTAIN speculative discussion, while peer reviewers acknowledge it as part of recognizing current limitations in their SUPPORTED novelty assessment.
Minimal overlap on claim C78 regarding prior work citations. OpenEval includes this in UNCERTAIN field assessment, while peer reviewers treat it as uncontested background in SUPPORTED category.
